deep.reconstruction:
This folio has no mathematics by Riemann. It is a printed (lithographed) sheet of geomagnetic observations that ended up in the bundle, probably as scrap paper; Riemann was living near Pisa in 1863. The sheet has two panels, each comparing three observatories for the day 5 July 1862 (5 Luglio 1862).

(1) Left panel, 'FORZA ORIZZONTALE' (horizontal magnetic force):
- Greenwich, local mean time (T.M. = tempo medio). Solid curve. Time axis runs 5h to 11h. The vertical scale runs from 0.1050 down to 0.1180 in steps of 0.0010; the intermediate ticks 60, 70, ..., 170 are abbreviations for 0.1060, ..., 0.1170. 'min.' is marked at the top and 'mass.' (massimo) at the bottom.
- The curve shows a disturbance. There is a sharp excursion toward 'mass.' around 5h45m to 6h. A rough climb toward the 'min.' side follows, with spikes, reaching a peak near 10h50m. Then comes a sudden reversal at about 11h.
- A dotted trace is overlaid on the Greenwich grid. It appears to be the Havana record re-plotted on the Greenwich time base.
- Havana, local mean time. Dotted curve. Time axis runs 23h to 6h; the scale is 0.00700 to 0.01000.
- Rome, local mean time. Dotted curve. Time axis runs 5h50m to 11h50m; the scale is 100 to 140 'Divisioni della Scala' (scale divisions).

(2) Right panel, 'DECLINAZIONE' (magnetic declination):
- Greenwich. Scale from 20°30' to 21°00'; time 6h to 12h. There are sharp oscillations near 7h, 8h and 8h40m, and a large spike at about 11h.
- Havana. Time 1h to 6h; scale in seconds of arc, labelled 215'' and 430'', with the top label read as 43''.
- Rome. Time 6h50m to 12h50m; scale 100 to 120 scale divisions. The Rome trace shows corresponding spikes near 8h40m and 11h40m.

Why the time axes are offset: the three axes are shifted by the longitude differences, so that the same physical instant lines up vertically. This is my inference, and it is consistent with the labels.
- Rome (Collegio Romano, longitude about 12°29' E) is about 50 minutes ahead of Greenwich. So 5h50m Rome time corresponds to about 5h00m Greenwich time.
- Havana (longitude about 82°21' W) is about 5h29m behind Greenwich. So 23h30m Havana time corresponds to about 5h Greenwich time.
- The purpose is to show that a magnetic disturbance (storm) was simultaneous at widely separated stations. This style matches A. Secchi's comparative magnetic publications from the Collegio Romano observatory in Rome.

The previous page's theta-function identities (for genus p = 4 and p = 5) do not continue here.
errors: No mathematical derivation is present, so there is nothing to check for errors.
The Havana declination labels (43'', 215'', 430'') are uneven as read. The top label may actually be 0'' or another value; this cannot be confirmed from the image.

results.what: Printed comparative plots of geomagnetic horizontal force and declination at Greenwich, Havana and Rome on 5 July 1862, with the time axes shifted by longitude to show that the disturbance was simultaneous
results.modern_name: Multi-station magnetogram comparison of a geomagnetic disturbance
results.usually_credited_to: Observatory publications of the period (likely A. Secchi, Collegio Romano, c. 1862-63)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a printed geomagnetic chart, not Riemann's work. Its presence among his papers fits his time in Italy (Pisa, 1863) and paper reuse. It contains no mathematical content attributable to him.

checkable.asserts: A longitude of about 12°29' E corresponds to about 49.9 minutes of time. This matches the roughly 50-minute shift of the Rome axis (5h50m Rome ≈ 5h Greenwich).
A longitude of about 82°21' W corresponds to about 5.49 hours. This matches the Havana axis offset (about 23h30m Havana ≈ 5h Greenwich).
The Greenwich force scale has 13 steps of 0.001 from 0.1050 to 0.1180, so the abbreviated ticks 60, ..., 170 mean 0.1060, ..., 0.1170. The expression equals 0.

transcription_corrections: '20.30'' should be read as 20°30' and '21.00' as 21°00' (degrees and minutes of declination).
The Greenwich force ticks '60, 70, ..., 170' are abbreviations for 0.1060 to 0.1170.
The next-page show-through is a mirror image of this sheet, so its date should be 5 Luglio 1862, not 1863.
The Havana declination label '43''' is doubtful and may be 0''.
